message.content:
At 10 kPa (≈ 0.1 bar) the pressure is well below the triple‑point pressure of water (≈ 61.16 kPa).  
Below the triple point the phase diagram shows that the solid–liquid equilibrium line continues downward with a negative slope.  
Using the Clausius–Clapeyron relation (or consulting standard phase‑diagram tables) gives a melting/freezing temperature of roughly **–2 °C** at 10 kPa.

In other words, at 10 kPa water would be frozen at temperatures above –2 °C and would melt only when the temperature rises above that value.
